description: The line plot illustrates the attack success rate (ASR) of three different trigger insertion strategies — “random,” “end,” and an unlabeled method represented by a green line with circle markers — across various target phrases on the SST-2 dataset under a clean-label poisoning setting with a 5% poison rate (2.6% of total data). The x-axis lists nine target phrases: “bb,” “mb,” “cf,” “beautiful,” “excellent,” “gorgeous,” “wonderful,” “brilliant,” “stunning,” and “beautifully,” arranged in that order with no numerical scale. The y-axis represents ASR, ranging from 0.2 to 0.9 in linear increments of 0.1. The green line (unlabeled) starts at ~0.2 for “bb,” peaks at ~0.74 for “mb,” dips to ~0.41 for “cf,” then rises steadily to ~0.91 at “stunning” before slightly declining to ~0.88 at “beautifully.” The orange line with “x” markers (“random”) begins at ~0.55 for “bb,” drops sharply to ~0.19 at “cf,” then climbs to ~0.85 at “gorgeous,” dips to ~0.64 at “wonderful,” and ends at ~0.89 for “beautifully.” The purple line with circle markers (“end”) starts at ~0.51 for “bb,” dips slightly to ~0.48 for “mb,” rises to ~0.84 for “cf,” fluctuates between ~0.65 and ~0.88 across subsequent phrases, and ends at ~0.85 for “beautifully.” All three lines show non-monotonic behavior, with the green line generally achieving the highest ASR across most phrases, particularly toward the end of the x-axis.
